title: High Strength and Fracture Resistance of Reduced-Activity W-Ta-Ti-V-Zr High-Entropy Alloy for Fusion Energy Applications.

recollection.starting_material: guess: high-purity elemental powders of W, Ta, Ti, V and Zr
recollection.intervention: guess: mechanical alloying of the powder blend followed by spark plasma sintering (or hot isostatic pressing) at ~1200–1400 °C
recollection.structure: guess: single-phase body-centered cubic (BCC) high-entropy solid solution with a dispersion of nanoscale precipitates enriched in Zr/Ti
recollection.mechanism: guess: severe lattice distortion and solid‐solution strengthening from a multicomponent BCC lattice, aided by fine precipitates that pin dislocations and reduce grain growth, combined with choice of low-activation elements to lower neutron-induced radioactivity
recollection.results: guess: room-temperature compressive/yield strength ~1.2–1.6 GPa, fracture toughness ~20–30 MPa·m^0.5, retention of >80% strength at 800 °C, and calculated neutron activation levels several times lower than standard W–Ta alloys

score.note: The recalled processing route is incorrect: the alloy was arc-melted and repeatedly remelted, not mechanically alloyed and SPS/HIP-consolidated. The proposed single-phase BCC matrix with nanoscale precipitates conflicts with the observed segregated two-BCC-phase dendritic structure. Solid-solution strengthening and lattice distortion are correctly recalled, but precipitate pinning and activation reduction were not established mechanisms in the reported results. The estimated room-temperature strength is reasonably close, but toughness is underestimated and the claimed 800 °C strength retention and activation values were not reported.
